paper_metadata.title: EEG and clinical predictors of medically intractable childhood epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the setting and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, as a retrospective study from a tertiary referral center, there is a high risk of selection bias toward more severe cases, which the authors acknowledge. The participation rate of the original 1000-patient pool is not fully transparent, as many were excluded for 'inadequate follow-up' without detailed counts.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Medical records were received from approximately 1000 children (,18 years) currently followed in the Division of Epilepsy and Clinical Neurophysiology at Children's Hospital in Boston.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as pediatric patients at a specific tertiary neurology division.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Because our study was a retrospective study and Children's Hospital is a tertiary referral hospital, our patient population may be biased toward including patients with severe epilepsy.
items.reasoning: While the recruitment method (chart review) is clear, the sampling frame is a convenience sample from a specialized center, which introduces inherent referral bias.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We included children who had been followed regularly for at least two years. Cases with shorter periods of follow-up or in which there was inadequate follow-up were excluded... We also excluded children who did not have EEGs as part of their initial evaluation.
items.reasoning: The authors provide specific criteria regarding follow-up duration, diagnostic requirements (2+ seizures), and data availability.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: We collected 144 cases of intractable cases and 39 cases of well-controlled cases from the above review of charts. The excluded cases were those patients in which seizure control did not meet the deønition of either intractable or well-controlled cases or in whom there was inadequate follow-up.
items.reasoning: It is unclear how many of the initial 1000 patients met the eligibility criteria versus how many were excluded due to missing data, making it difficult to assess participation bias.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 2 Characteristics of intractable and well-controlled group... Age of seizure onset (mean, year), Age of first EEG (mean, year), F/U duration (mean, year), Male sex (%).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study excludes a large portion of the initial cohort due to 'inadequate follow-up.' Because the characteristics of these excluded patients are not compared to the included sample, there is a risk of attrition bias, although the included patients had a stable mean follow-up of ~5 years.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis

items.reasoning: Only 183 out of approximately 1000 records (18.3%) were included in the final analysis. This is a high rate of exclusion.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (EEG and clinical features) are well-defined using standard neurological criteria (International 10-20 system, Blume 1982). While retrospective, the use of objective EEG data and standardized clinical definitions limits measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Diffuse slowing was deøned as slower than expected background frequencies for the patient's age (Blume, 1982)... Asymmetrical background was deøned as a 50% or greater difference in amplitude.
items.reasoning: The authors provide explicit, quantitative definitions for the EEG prognostic factors.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Electroencephalogram recordings were obtained with a 21 channel electroencephalograph, employing scalp electrodes placed according to the international 10-20 system.
items.reasoning: Standardized, internationally recognized methods for EEG recording and interpretation were used.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Frequency of spikes or sharp waves was coded as greater or less than 1 per 60 s.
items.reasoning: The authors used pre-defined cut-points for EEG frequencies and clinical ages.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: While the majority of children were initially evaluated at Children's Hospital, we included some cases who had their þrst EEG elsewhere if the clinical information and laboratory studies were reliable and adequate.
items.reasoning: Most were done at one center, but some external EEGs were included, introducing slight potential for variability.

items.reasoning: The study design ensured that all included participants had the primary prognostic factor (EEG) available.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (intractability vs. well-controlled) is clearly defined based on clinical response to a specific number of AEDs and a minimum duration of seizure freedom. These are standard, though slightly arbitrary, clinical endpoints.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Medical intractability was deøned as continued seizures despite adequate trials of 3 or more antiepileptic drugs (AEDs)... Well-controlled epilepsy was deøned as having no seizures for a minimum of one year.
items.reasoning: The outcome categories are explicitly defined with clear clinical thresholds.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: A trial of AEDs was considered adequate if, in the opinion of the child's neurologist, the dosage was increased until there was either seizure control or signs of clinical or laboratory toxicity.
items.reasoning: Outcome was determined by specialist neurologists based on clinical and laboratory data, which is the clinical standard.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Information was abstracted retrospectively from the child's medical records. To obtain missing information, the child's neurologist was contacted.
items.reasoning: The same criteria and data collection methods were applied to both the intractable and well-controlled groups.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable logistic regression to adjust for several key confounders (age, etiology, seizure type). However, because it is a retrospective study, some potential confounders (like specific treatment protocols or socioeconomic factors) may not have been fully captured or adjusted for.

The authors used both univariate and multivariate models and were transparent about excluding certain variables (like Lennox-Gastaut) from the multivariate model due to zero cells, which is a correct statistical practice.
